LanguageData.AB_VerboseLoggingTip: Write detailed diagnostic messages to the log. Only useful when hunting a bug.
LanguageData.AB_NotLinkedLine: Not connected to another level yet.
LanguageData.AB_ViewOtherLevelDesc: Jump the camera to the connected stairwell on the other level. You can also press Page Up and Page Down to switch levels.
LanguageData.AB_BasementCreated: The basement level has been opened. It is solid rock, mine it out to expand.
LanguageData.AB_SkyCreated: The sky level has been opened. Build floors above roofed rooms to expand upward.
LanguageData.AB_OnlySurfaceForNow: Must be placed on the surface level.
LanguageData.AB_LevelCap: Level limit reached (one above, one below).
LanguageData.AB_ShowLiveBelow: Show live movement on the level below
LanguageData.AB_ShowLiveBelowTip: Draw pawns, animals, and projectiles from the level below when looking down through open air. Turn off if you want a small performance gain on the sky level.
LanguageData.AB_SelectBelowInPlace: Select pawns on the level below
LanguageData.AB_SelectBelowInPlaceTip: Click a pawn visible through open air on the level below to select it without leaving the sky view. Requires showing live movement on the level below.
LanguageData.AB_BelowDimTip: How much the view of the level below is darkened when seen from above. Kept low by default: the ground below staying bright and visible is part of what makes the upper level read as raised rather than the gap reading as a pit.
LanguageData.AB_SlabEdgeTip: Rooftop and floor edges that border open air get a thin dark outline, so slab borders read as clean seams instead of raw texture boundaries.
LanguageData.AB_WallRevealTip: The outer ring of rooftop tiles shows a strip of the supporting wall's top along edges that border open air, so the roof reads as resting on the wall line below instead of floating. Covered by anything built on the rim.
LanguageData.AB_WallRevealWidthTip: How much of the outer rooftop tile shows the wall underneath, in cells.
LanguageData.AB_BelowScaleTip: Pawns, animals, items, plants, and furniture on the level below draw smaller than life size, mimicking the zoom out of looking down a full story. Every object shrinks in place on its own cell, so nothing slides or misaligns. Walls and other connected structures keep their true size.
LanguageData.AB_GenNote: Generation settings apply when a level is first created. Existing sky and basement levels keep the look they were generated with.
LanguageData.AB_PresetsTip: One-click looks for newly generated mountain peaks. Default restores every generation setting; the others adjust the peak sliders below and leave ore and cavern settings alone.
LanguageData.AB_PlateauOpennessTip: How much of the mountain's deep interior opens into walkable meadow plateau instead of solid rock. Low values give craggy, mostly-solid peaks; high values give broad open highlands.
LanguageData.AB_MeadowScaleTip: The scale of the meadow pattern. High values carve a few large connected meadows; low values scatter many small pockets and winding rock fingers.
LanguageData.AB_TerraceMaxTip: The deepest the walkable rock terrace along the mountain edge can cut into the mass, in cells. 1 is the classic single ledge; higher values open wide shelf stretches.
LanguageData.AB_OutcropDensityTip: How many rocky outcrop mounts stud the open plateaus. 0% removes them entirely.
LanguageData.AB_TarnsTip: Small tarns pooled on the open plateau, with deep water at the heart of the larger ones. 0% keeps the plateau dry.
LanguageData.AB_HiddenValleysTip: The share of fully rock-enclosed meadow pockets that stay sealed and unexplored (hidden valleys). The rest are breached with a narrow walkable notch and generate as reachable canyon meadows instead.
LanguageData.AB_SkyOreTip: Ore lumps per 10,000 mountain mass cells on newly generated sky levels.
LanguageData.AB_BasementOreTip: Ore lumps per 10,000 cells in newly generated basement rock.
LanguageData.AB_ChamberFreqTip: How often the cavern network widens into a large chamber, per carve step (shown as a percentage). Chambers are also where the cavern biome's own lakes and terrain features tend to land, so raise this for wetter, roomier caverns.
LanguageData.AB_CavernFormationsTip: Density of stalagmites and other Biomes! Caverns formations in generated caverns. 0% skips them entirely.
LanguageData.AB_PreviewNote: Illustrative sample - real peaks follow your actual mountains.
LanguageData.AB_SkyLandmarksTip: Newly generated sky levels can host landmarks - ancient smoke vents, monuments, and other features from the Odyssey landmark system, including landmarks added by mods such as Vanilla Landmarks Expanded. Landmarks need real mountain ground: they only appear on levels with an open plateau at least 7x7 clear, and their structures are confined to the plateau. Applies when a sky level is first generated.
LanguageData.AB_LandmarkChanceTip: The chance that a newly generated sky level with open plateau ground rolls one landmark from the pool of landmarks set to Random.
LanguageData.AB_LandmarkMaxTip: The most landmarks one sky level can receive, counting forced, enabled, and randomly rolled ones together.
LanguageData.AB_LandmarksNeedOdyssey: Landmarks on sky levels require the Odyssey expansion.
LanguageData.AB_GuardPanelTip: Every subsystem runs behind its own kill switch: if one hits an error it shuts itself down so the rest of the mod and your game keep running. Tripped subsystems are listed here and can be re-armed; they also reset when a game is loaded.
LanguageData.AB_GuardTripped: {0} - shut down after an error in {1}
LanguageData.AB_ResetAllConfirm: Reset every setting on every tab to its default value?
LanguageData.AB_SkyBiomeInheritTip: Newly created sky levels use the same biome as the surface map below, so plateau soil, greenery, tree regrowth, wild plant mix, and weather match the world around the mountain - including modded biomes, whose own fertile terrain and plants carry up to the peak. Applies when a sky level is first generated; existing sky levels keep the biome they were created with. Off restores the stark high-altitude look.
LanguageData.AB_ClimbTimeTip: Multiplies how long every stairs type takes to climb. Ladders are slower and grand staircases faster than normal stairs regardless.
LanguageData.AB_ShowCeilingHint: Show ceiling hints on the surface
LanguageData.AB_ShowCeilingHintTip: Cells under a built sky level floor draw a faint ceiling texture, so you can tell there is a structure overhead while looking at the surface.
LanguageData.AB_StairsCollapsed: A stairwell lost its support and collapsed.
LanguageData.AB_DismountFirst: Dismount before using stairs or elevators.
LanguageData.AB_GoUpDesc: Take the nearest stairs to the level above.
LanguageData.AB_GoDownDesc: Take the nearest stairs to the level below.
LanguageData.AB_NoStairs: no linked stairs on this level
LanguageData.AB_LinkBlocked: The stairwell could not connect. The matching spot on the other level is blocked.
LanguageData.AB_BlockedOnTarget: The matching spot on the other level is blocked.
LanguageData.AB_NoSupportOnTarget: The matching spot on the other level cannot support a stairwell.
LanguageData.AB_CrossLevelOrdersTip: When you right-click to command a pawn selected on the level below, they walk to the nearest stairs, ride up, and then carry out the order at the chosen spot on this level. Covers drafted moves, attacks, hauling, and work orders.
LanguageData.AB_CrossLevelCombatTip: Drafted colonists ordered to attack an enemy on the level below (or above), seen through open air, fire straight across the gap when they have a clear line and the target is in range - plunging or rising fire lands on the other level with normal accuracy and damage. When there is no open line of fire, or the target is out of range or in the basement, they instead take the stairs and engage on that level.
LanguageData.AB_CrossLevelAutoEngage: Pawns fire across the gap on their own
LanguageData.AB_CrossLevelAutoEngageTip: Enemies with ranged weapons and no reachable target on their own level shoot up or down through open air at your pawns, and your drafted colonists with fire at will enabled return fire across the gap without being ordered. Turn off to make cross-level shooting player-ordered only.
LanguageData.AB_MortarTargetSet: {0} will bombard the target on the other level whenever it is manned, loaded, and free of local threats.
LanguageData.AB_NoArcPath: No open path for the shell between levels.
LanguageData.AB_TurretTargetSet: {0} will fire at the target on the other level whenever it is ready and free of local threats.
LanguageData.AB_NoGapLine: No clear line of fire through the gap.
LanguageData.AB_GapLineLost: {0} lost its line of fire to the other level.
LanguageData.AB_StopCrossBombardTip: Cancel this turret's bombardment order on the other level.
LanguageData.AB_AnimalWanderTip: Wild animals treat stairwells as part of the landscape: one occasionally wanders down into the basement to shelter, lingers a while, and leaves again - and any wild animal stuck on a level with nothing to eat finds its way back to the surface. Pen and colony animals never wander on their own, and nothing wanders up to the sky level by itself.
LanguageData.AB_CrossLevelRituals: Rituals summon participants from other levels
LanguageData.AB_CrossLevelRitualsTip: Ritual role holders and participants on linked levels count as available: starting the ritual first sends everyone off-level to the stairs, and the ceremony begins the moment they all arrive. A gather that cannot complete (a participant dies, the stairs are destroyed) cancels after a few hours.
LanguageData.AB_CrossLevelSocial: Linked levels count as one colony
LanguageData.AB_CrossLevelSocialTip: Pawns on another level of the same column still count as together and at home. Psychic bonds (including Highmates) skip the bond distance penalty within a column, and sky and basement levels report as part of the player colony, so vanilla and modded "away from the colony" checks treat everyone as home. Per-map alerts and quest map selection keep vanilla behavior.
LanguageData.AB_RitualGathering: {0} ritual participant(s) are taking the stairs. The ceremony begins when everyone arrives.
LanguageData.AB_RitualGatherTimeout: The gathering for {0} took too long and was called off.
LanguageData.AB_RitualNoRoute: {0} has no stair route to the ritual.
LanguageData.AB_CrossLevelWork: Colonists take stairs to work on other levels
LanguageData.AB_CrossLevelWorkTip: When a colonist finds no work on their current level, they check directly linked levels and take the stairs if there is something to do there.
LanguageData.AB_PriorityCrossLevelWorkTip: Colonists also check other levels while they still have work here: if a linked level holds work of strictly higher priority (by their work settings), they take the stairs for it instead of settling for the lower-priority local job. A warden set to priority 1 will leave priority-2 mining to go tend the prisoners in the basement. Equal-priority work always stays local, and results are cached so the extra checks stay cheap.
LanguageData.AB_IdleReturnHome: Idle colonists return to the surface
LanguageData.AB_IdleReturnHomeTip: Colonists with nothing to do on any level head back down to the surface instead of roaming the level they worked on.
LanguageData.AB_CrossLevelHaulingTip: When an item's best storage is on another level, haulers carry it through the stairs. Runs after normal hauling on the same level.
LanguageData.AB_CrossLevelSupply: Fetch needed materials from other levels
LanguageData.AB_CrossLevelSupplyTip: When a level needs materials it does not have - construction materials for blueprints and frames, ingredients for bills, or meals for patients and prisoners - a colonist takes the stairs to a linked level that has them and carries them back. Covers the case where the resources sit in a stockpile on another level and no idle hauler is standing there to push them across.
LanguageData.AB_CrossLevelNeeds: Colonists cross levels to sleep in their beds
LanguageData.AB_CrossLevelNeedsTip: A tired colonist whose bed is on another level takes the stairs instead of sleeping on the ground.
LanguageData.AB_CrossLevelPrisonersTip: When a prisoner's only usable cell is on another level, or you have assigned them a bed on another level, a warden carries them through the stairs to it. You can also right-click a prisoner to send them to a cell above or below.
LanguageData.AB_RemoveLinkDesc: Mark this for removal. A builder will deconstruct it, which also removes the linked end on the other level. Vertical links cannot be damaged, so this is the only way to get rid of them.
LanguageData.AB_ColumnWealthTip: The storyteller counts wealth and pawns on all your levels, not just the surface. Prevents hiding wealth from raid scaling in the basement. Recommended on for honest difficulty.
LanguageData.AB_WorldIntegrationTip: Caravans can include colonists from other levels (they take the stairs to join the gathering), transport pods and shuttles can launch from the sky level, trade beacons on any level sell their goods, and comms consoles work below ground.
LanguageData.AB_CaravanNeedsSurfacePawn: Caravans must form on the surface: include at least one colonist who is on the surface level.
LanguageData.AB_CaravanPawnNoStairs: {0} cannot reach any stairs to the surface and will not join the caravan.
LanguageData.AB_CaravanPawnsDescending: {0} colonist(s) are taking the stairs to join the caravan.
LanguageData.AB_AbandonLevelsWarning: {0} colonist(s) are still on other levels of this colony. Abandoning the settlement destroys every level with it, and they will be lost. Are you sure?
LanguageData.AB_PodTransit: Drop pods fall through sky-level gaps
LanguageData.AB_PodTransitTip: Incoming drop pods, ship chunks and meteorites bound for the surface pass through the sky level's airspace when there is an open gap above their landing spot. While they cross the upper level, anti-air defenses built up there can engage them. Landing spot, descent time and impact effects are unchanged. Shuttles and anything landing on the sky level itself are unaffected. On by default.
LanguageData.AB_ThreatBasementInfestTip: When an infestation fires at your colony, it has a chance to burrow up into the basement level instead of the surface. Threat size and storyteller pacing are unchanged; only the battlefield moves. Off by default.
LanguageData.AB_ThreatSkyDrops: Drop-pod raids can target the sky level
LanguageData.AB_ThreatSkyDropsTip: When a hostile drop-pod raid fires at your colony, it has a chance to land on your rooftops instead of the surface. Raiders who find nothing to fight up there will take your stairs down. Threat size and storyteller pacing are unchanged. Off by default.
LanguageData.AB_ThreatDivertChanceTip: The chance that an eligible incident is diverted to another level instead of hitting the surface.
LanguageData.AB_TakePrisonerUpTo: Take {0} to a cell on the level above
LanguageData.AB_TakePrisonerDownTo: Take {0} to a cell on the level below
LanguageData.AB_ExtendUpDesc: Extend the elevator shaft to the level above, opening it if needed, and place a linked car there.
LanguageData.AB_ExtendDownDesc: Extend the elevator shaft to the level below, opening it if needed, and place a linked car there.
LanguageData.AB_LevelWidgetTip: You can also press Page Up and Page Down.
LanguageData.AB_ShowLevelWidgetTip: Adds view level above and view level below buttons next to the other view toggles in the bottom right.
LanguageData.AB_OneColonistBar: Merge each column into one colonist bar group
LanguageData.AB_OneColonistBarTip: Draw the sky, surface, and basement of a single column as one continuous block on the colonist bar, with no separator gap between the levels. Other colonies and caravans keep their own groups. Defers to [LTO] Colony Groups when that mod is active.
LanguageData.AB_CameraFollowStairsTip: When you send a selected colonist up or down stairs (or an elevator), the view rides along to the level they arrive on, centered on them at the same zoom. Only follows the pawn you have selected and are watching - autonomous haulers, pets, and enemies never move your camera.
LanguageData.AB_GridLinkReceiving: Grid link: receiving {0} W from the connected level.
LanguageData.AB_GridLinkSending: Grid link: sending {0} W to the connected level.
LanguageData.AB_GridLinkIdle: Grid link: connected, no flow needed.
LanguageData.AB_CrossLevelPipesTip: When pipes from Dubs Bad Hygiene or a Vanilla Expanded pipe network touch a linked stairwell on both levels, their stored contents flow between the levels. Power conduits connect through stairwells regardless of this setting.
LanguageData.AB_CrossLevelTemperatureTip: Linked stairwells slowly equalize temperature between the rooms they stand in, like a vent between floors. The sky level also follows the surface's outdoor temperature and seasons.
LanguageData.AB_CameraLockKeybindTip: Enables the camera level lock hotkey (End by default, rebindable under Options - Keyboard configuration). While the lock is on, the camera stays on the level you are viewing: it will not ride along when a selected pawn takes the stairs. Manual level switching always works.
LanguageData.AB_CameraLockOn: Camera level lock ON: the view stays on this level. Press the hotkey again to release.
LanguageData.AB_CameraLockOff: Camera level lock off: the camera follows pawns through stairs again.
LanguageData.AB_CavernBasements: Basements generate as living caverns (Biomes! Caverns)
LanguageData.AB_CavernBasementsTip: Newly generated basements come out as one of Biomes! Caverns' cave biomes: a connected tunnel network with cave terrain, flora, wildlife, stalagmites and crystals, sealed inside the rock until you break into it. Existing basements are unchanged. Note: the earthen depths biome is constantly hot.
LanguageData.AB_CavernBiomeTip: Which cave biome new basements use. Random picks per basement, weighted toward fungal forest; earthen depths is rare because its constant 55C heat makes a punishing basement.
LanguageData.AB_CavernOpennessTip: How much of the basement the tunnel network carves out. Low keeps most of the level as mineable rock with occasional caves; high makes a sprawling open cave system.
LanguageData.AB_NaturalPeaks: Naturalistic mountain peaks on new sky levels
LanguageData.AB_NaturalPeaksTip: Mountain tops on newly generated sky levels come out as walkable highland plateaus: natural terrain with patches of soil and vegetation, rocky outcrops, and a cliff rim of solid rock whose depth wanders naturally. Off restores the classic fully solid peak. Existing sky levels are unchanged either way.
LanguageData.AB_PeakSoilTip: How much of the plateau surface is fertile soil you can farm, as opposed to gravel and bare rock.
LanguageData.AB_PeakVegetationTip: Density of wild plants and trees seeded on the plateau at generation, relative to the surface biome's normal density. Regrowth afterwards is natural.
LanguageData.AB_ClimbAnimations: Climb animations on stairs and ladders
LanguageData.AB_ClimbAnimationsTip: While climbing stairs or a ladder, pawns visibly step onto the flight and sink into it going down, or rise out of it going up, with a short emerging flourish on the other level. Elevators are unaffected. Purely cosmetic.
LanguageData.AB_JobsNote: How eagerly pawns look for cross-level work. Faster scanning feels more responsive but costs a little performance in big colonies. Defaults match the tuned built-in cadence.
LanguageData.AB_JobsPresetsTip: One-click cadence profiles. Relaxed halves the scanning effort, Eager doubles it, Frantic is for small colonies that want near-instant cross-level reactions. The sliders below show what each preset sets.
LanguageData.AB_JobProbeBudgetTip: How many cross-level work checks the whole colony may run per game tick. Higher means pawns notice work on other levels sooner; each probe is a bounded virtual scan.
LanguageData.AB_JobEmptyScanCooldownTip: How long a pawn waits before checking other levels again after a fruitless cross-level scan. Lower means quicker reactions to new work appearing elsewhere.
LanguageData.AB_JobMigrationCooldownTip: Minimum time a pawn stays put after migrating to another level for work, so pawns do not ping-pong up and down the stairs. Fresh player designations bypass this.
LanguageData.AB_JobCacheTtlTip: How long per-level summaries of available work and needed materials stay cached before a rebuild. New blueprints and designations refresh these instantly regardless.
LanguageData.AB_SupplyConstruction: Builders carry materials to other levels
LanguageData.AB_SupplyConstructionTip: Pawns doing construction work ferry needed building materials through the stairs to blueprints and frames on linked levels, then build there.
LanguageData.AB_SupplyBillsTip: Workbenches with active bills register ingredient shortfalls so haulers top the level up from linked levels.
LanguageData.AB_SupplyMeals: Pull meals for patients and prisoners
LanguageData.AB_SupplyMealsTip: Levels with bedridden patients or prisoners keep a small buffer of meals pulled from linked levels, so doctors and wardens feed locally.
LanguageData.AB_FetchFromOtherLevelsTip: Idle haulers check directly linked levels for haul work and go get it, instead of waiting for the slower idle-migration drift.
